caption: Fig. 2. Overlap-tile strategy for seamless segmentation of arbitrary large images (here segmentation of neuronal structures in EM stacks). Prediction of the segmentation in the yellow area, requires image data within the blue area as input. Missing input data is extrapolated by mirroring
description:
Figure Description: The figure illustrates the overlap-tile strategy for seamless segmentation of large images, specifically for segmenting neuronal structures in electron microscopy (EM) stacks. It shows two panels connected by a green arrow, indicating the process flow. The left panel displays a segmented image with a yellow highlighted area, representing the region of interest for prediction. The right panel shows a zoomed-in view of the highlighted area, with a blue box indicating the input data required for the prediction. The figure caption mentions that missing input data is extrapolated by mirroring.

Text in Figure: Overlap-tile strategy, segmentation of neuronal structures, EM stacks, prediction, yellow area, blue area, input data, extrapolation, mirroring.

caption: Fig. 3. HeLa cells on glass recorded with DIC (differential interference contrast) microscopy. ( a ) raw image. ( b ) overlay with ground truth segmentation. Different colors indicate different instances of the HeLa cells. ( c ) generated segmentation mask (white: foreground, black: background). ( d ) map with a pixel-wise loss weight to force the network to learn the border pixels.
description:
## Description
This figure displays four panels of images related to the segmentation of HeLa cells using U-Net. Panel (a) shows a raw image of HeLa cells. Panel (b) overlays the raw image with ground truth segmentation, where different colors represent different instances of HeLa cells. Panel (c) presents the generated segmentation mask, with white indicating the foreground and black the background. Panel (d) shows a map with pixel-wise loss weights, highlighting the border pixels.

## Text in figure
Panel (a): raw image
Panel (b): overlay with ground truth segmentation
Panel (c): generated segmentation mask
Panel (d): map with pixel-wise loss weight
Colors in Panel (b): different instances of HeLa cells
White in Panel (c): foreground
Black in Panel (c): background
Map in Panel (d): pixel-wise loss weight
